focus: Burst-friendly m_axi access, 512-bit widening, and matching lane-wide compute.
merge_rule: Union of gemm_flatten_v1 and flash_no_RMW overlay. On id conflicts, the no-RMW overlay replaces the v1 entry.

guards: do not change top-level pointer element types unless explicitly allowed
do not treat adding m_axi pragmas as complete coalescing
confirm accesses are contiguous and burst-friendly
only unroll lane computation when iterations are independent or safely reducible
handle N not divisible by the lane factor
skills.pattern: m_axi port feeds a contiguous streaming loop, the active host/testbench contract expects the original scalar pointer types, and memory bandwidth limits performance
required_steps: add max_widen_bitwidth=512 to relevant m_axi ports
use burst length and outstanding transaction pragmas
stage contiguous global-memory regions into local buffers where helpful
compute LANES = 512 / element_bitwidth
rewrite the compute loop to process multiple lanes per outer iteration when legal
partition local lane buffers to match the lane factor
validate csim/cosim and inspect synthesis reports for burst/widening success
skills.strategy: preserve the public scalar pointer ABI; request 512-bit automatic m_axi widening with max_widen_bitwidth=512; use burst/outstanding pragmas; stage contiguous data into local buffers; pipeline load/store loops; and rewrite the compute loop to process LANES = 512 / element_bitwidth elements per memory beat when iterations are independent

guards: do not change the host ABI unless explicitly allowed
wide memory movement alone is insufficient if compute remains scalar
lane-level compute unrolling requires independent iterations or a safe reduction structure
watch DSP/LUT/BRAM growth after increasing lane parallelism
skills.pattern: m_axi port feeds a pipelined loop, latency remains bandwidth dominated, and synthesis/report evidence shows narrow or failed burst/widening behavior
required_steps: request or implement 512-bit memory movement
rewrite load/store loops to be burst-friendly
unpack/stage lanes into local buffers
unroll lane-level compute
partition local buffers by lane factor
handle tails and alignment safely
skills.strategy: request 512-bit m_axi widening using max_widen_bitwidth=512; if a packed wide-bus ABI is explicitly allowed, use ap_uint<512> words; in both cases, unpack/stage into lane-partitioned local buffers and rewrite computation to exploit parallel lanes rather than continuing scalar one-element-at-a-time compute

skills.pattern: UNROLL by factor UF on a loop that reads/writes local arrays without enough parallel memory ports
skills.strategy: Apply ARRAY_PARTITION (cyclic or complete) so local arrays expose enough read/write ports for the unroll factor. Complete partition for small partial-sum arrays; cyclic factor=UF for lane buffers.
required_steps: identify unroll factor UF on hot loop
count simultaneous array accesses per unrolled iteration
add #pragma HLS ARRAY_PARTITION with factor matching UF or complete for small arrays
verify csynth does not report memory port conflicts on locals
guards: watch BRAM/LUT growth from complete partition on large arrays
partition dim must match access pattern (row vs column)
do not treat interface pragmas alone as complete coalescing
do not change top-level pointer types unless explicitly allowed
do not unroll lane computation if there is a true loop-carried dependence
for reductions, use partial sums or a tree reduction instead of a single serial accumulator
watch DSP/LUT/BRAM growth after lane parallelism
skills.pattern: the kernel is bandwidth-sensitive, accesses contiguous global memory through m_axi ports, and has per-element or lane-independent computation that can be parallelized after widening memory transfers
required_steps: add max_widen_bitwidth=512 to relevant m_axi ports
use max_read_burst_length/max_write_burst_length and outstanding transaction pragmas where appropriate
rewrite global accesses to be contiguous, monotonic, and unit-stride where possible
separate load, compute, and store if mixed logic blocks burst inference
compute LANES = 512 / element_bitwidth
process LANES elements per outer-loop iteration
unroll the lane loop when iterations are independent
partition local lane buffers to match the lane factor
handle non-multiple tails and boundary conditions
validate csim/cosim and inspect reports for burst and widening success
skills.strategy: apply coalescing as a full transformation: request 512-bit m_axi widening with max_widen_bitwidth=512, rewrite global-memory access into burst-friendly contiguous load/store loops, stage data into local lane buffers, and restructure computation to process multiple elements per widened memory beat using lane-level unrolling and matching buffer partitioning

guards: only apply to independent iterations or safely transformed reductions
do not duplicate memory reads if local staging can feed all lane operations
avoid excessive lane factor if resource utilization exceeds limits
skills.pattern: m_axi widening or burst bandwidth improves memory movement, but the compute loop still processes one scalar element per iteration and does not exploit the wider memory beat
required_steps: identify element bitwidth
set LANES = 512 / element_bitwidth
group scalar iterations into base + lane form
unroll the lane loop
partition local lane buffers completely or cyclically by lane factor
handle tails with idx < N guards or a cleanup loop
skills.strategy: rewrite the compute loop around a lane factor equal to 512 divided by element bitwidth; unroll the lane loop; partition local lane buffers; and perform multiple independent scalar operations per outer-loop iteration

guards: do not introduce out-of-bounds accesses
do not reorder writes when observable output order matters
do not assume indirect indexed accesses can be coalesced without a layout rewrite
skills.pattern: global-memory accesses are logically contiguous but written with mixed compute, conditional control, irregular indexing, or non-monotonic loop structure that prevents burst inference or automatic port widening
required_steps: isolate global-memory load and store loops
make addresses monotonic and unit-stride where legal
pipeline load and store loops
stage data in local buffers if compute is irregular
preserve boundary conditions and output order
skills.strategy: rewrite memory access into clean unit-stride load/store loops, separate irregular compute from global memory access when useful, and stage data into local buffers before compute

guards: floating-point associativity changes can alter bit-exact results
only use if the test tolerance or algorithm permits reassociation
for bit-exact reductions, keep serial order or use a guarded mode
skills.pattern: the widened memory beat provides multiple scalar elements per cycle, but the computation is a reduction with a serial accumulator that prevents lane-level parallelism
required_steps: compute LANES = 512 / element_bitwidth
create lane-local partial accumulators
unroll lane updates
combine partial accumulators through a tree or final reduction loop
preserve numerical tolerance expectations for floating-point reductions
skills.strategy: replace the serial accumulator with lane-local partial sums or a reduction tree so multiple elements from each widened memory beat can be consumed in parallel

guards: avoid complete partitioning large arrays
verify that partitioning resolves II without excessive LUT/FF growth
skills.pattern: lane-level compute is introduced after 512-bit coalescing, but local buffers still have insufficient memory ports to feed all lanes in parallel
required_steps: identify local buffers consumed by the unrolled lane loop
match partition factor to lane or unroll factor
prefer complete partition for small lane buffers
prefer cyclic partition for larger arrays with regular lane indexing
skills.strategy: partition local lane buffers completely or cyclically by the lane/unroll factor so all unrolled lane operations can read/write without BRAM port conflicts

skills.pattern: kernel has two or more m_axi pointer ports and uses #pragma HLS DATAFLOW or multiple load/compute/store tasks that should overlap external memory access
skills.strategy: Assign a distinct bundle=gmem0, gmem1, … to each m_axi pointer port so HLS can issue concurrent external memory transactions across DATAFLOW stages. Never place all read/write ports on a single bundle=gmem when stages are meant to run concurrently.
required_steps: enumerate every m_axi port on the top kernel and on DATAFLOW subfunctions that touch global memory
assign each pointer port a unique bundle=gmemN (gmem0, gmem1, gmem2, …)
map load tasks to read ports and store tasks to write ports on separate bundles when stages overlap
re-run csynth and verify parallel tasks no longer stall on a single gmem port (HLS 200-885 on gmem)
pair with hls::stream or proven stage overlap — distinct bundles alone do not fix decorative DATAFLOW
guards: each bundle still needs burst-friendly access patterns on its port
do not duplicate bundle names across unrelated ports
cosim and interface pragmas must stay consistent after rebundling
skills.template:
// BAD: all ports share one bundle — DATAFLOW tasks serialize on gmem
#pragma HLS INTERFACE m_axi port=A bundle=gmem
#pragma HLS INTERFACE m_axi port=B bundle=gmem
#pragma HLS INTERFACE m_axi port=y bundle=gmem

// GOOD: one bundle per port for concurrent stage access
#pragma HLS INTERFACE m_axi port=A bundle=gmem0
#pragma HLS INTERFACE m_axi port=B bundle=gmem1
#pragma HLS INTERFACE m_axi port=y bundle=gmem2

guards: do not move ports without updating host/linker bank assignment if needed
do not split dependent streams in a way that complicates correctness
ensure the chosen platform actually has multiple memory banks
skills.pattern: one memory bundle or bank carries most of the traffic while other banks are unused or underused
required_steps: estimate memory traffic by port
identify independent streams that can move banks
separate high-read and high-write streams when useful
update m_axi bundle names and host/linker mapping
validate performance and correctness
skills.strategy: redistribute independent arrays, read-only tables, or output streams across available memory banks so traffic is balanced and concurrent accesses avoid contention

guards: do not split arrays that must remain on the same physical memory for host compatibility
do not assume bundle names alone map to separate banks without platform/linker support
avoid bank imbalance where one bank remains the bottleneck
skills.pattern: multiple high-bandwidth arrays or streams are accessed independently but share one memory bundle or memory bank, creating bandwidth contention
required_steps: identify independent high-bandwidth arrays
estimate read/write traffic per array
place independent streams on separate m_axi bundles
map bundles to distinct physical banks if platform/host supports it
update host-side buffer bank assignment if required
verify bandwidth and correctness
skills.strategy: assign independent high-bandwidth m_axi ports to separate bundles or memory banks so concurrent memory streams can use independent bandwidth
skills.template:
#pragma HLS INTERFACE m_axi port=A offset=slave bundle=gmem0
#pragma HLS INTERFACE m_axi port=B offset=slave bundle=gmem1
#pragma HLS INTERFACE m_axi port=C offset=slave bundle=gmem2
// Ensure host/linker maps gmem0/gmem1/gmem2 to distinct memory banks when required.

guards: do not prefetch indirect or data-dependent addresses unless correctness and bounds are guaranteed
prefetch depth must fit local memory and avoid FIFO deadlock
outstanding transaction pragmas may not help if access pattern is non-burstable
preserve ordering when memory side effects or aliasing matter
skills.pattern: the compute pipeline stalls waiting for global-memory responses even though future addresses are known early enough to prefetch or issue longer bursts
required_steps: confirm future read addresses are predictable before data is consumed
rewrite accesses to monotonic contiguous bursts when legal
create a local prefetch buffer, FIFO, or tile cache with bounded depth
pipeline the prefetch loop and the compute loop separately
set num_read_outstanding and max_read_burst_length on relevant m_axi ports
guard prefetch distance, tails, and bounds
inspect reports for actual burst inference and outstanding behavior
skills.strategy: issue burst-friendly prefetches into a local queue, stream, or tile buffer ahead of compute; increase safe outstanding transactions and burst length so memory latency is hidden behind local computation

guards: do not stage unbounded arrays into local memory
DATAFLOW requires legal producer/consumer structure and bounded stream behavior
do not change host ABI or pointer types unless explicitly allowed
if each element is used once and access is already streaming, staging should still enable burst/dataflow or it may add overhead
skills.pattern: a pipelined compute loop directly issues m_axi/gmem reads and immediately consumes the response, or directly writes results, so request/response latency or AXI scheduling prevents low II
required_steps: identify m_axi reads/writes inside the II-limited compute loop
split global load, compute, and global store into separate loops or functions
make load/store addresses contiguous and burst-friendly where possible
stage bounded chunks into local buffers or streams
apply DATAFLOW at the parent scope when stages can run concurrently
use ping-pong buffers for tiled/chunked stages when the same buffer would serialize load and compute
set appropriate burst length and outstanding transaction pragmas where legal
pipeline compute over local memory and validate burst/report behavior
skills.strategy: decouple global-memory request/response from compute by splitting load, compute, and store stages; use burst-friendly load/store loops, local buffers or hls::stream FIFOs, DATAFLOW, and optionally ping-pong buffering to keep compute working on local data

guards: do not interchange loops when it violates data dependencies or output order
manual loop interchange is not useful if the tool already performs it and no access pattern changes
after reordering, partition the dimension actually accessed in parallel
verify boundaries and row-major/column-major indexing carefully
skills.pattern: a loop nest misses II because the innermost pipelined loop uses strided/non-contiguous global accesses, repeatedly hits the same local memory bank, or places the dependency-carrying dimension in the hot pipeline
required_steps: identify current inner-loop memory stride and dependency direction
determine whether loop interchange or strip-mining preserves semantics
choose an inner dimension with contiguous global access or conflict-free bank mapping
update local buffer layout and ARRAY_PARTITION dim to match the new inner loop
rewrite index expressions and boundary/tail handling
pipeline the new hot loop and inspect burst/II reports
skills.strategy: reorder or strip-mine loops so the pipelined inner loop is unit-stride for global memory, maps parallel lanes to distinct local banks, or moves true dependencies to an outer sequential dimension when legal

guards: do not apply when the operation is order-sensitive or non-associative under required correctness checks
floating-point results may differ from serial accumulation due to reassociation
ensure input bandwidth can feed the chosen lane factor
do not suppress the true accumulator dependence with a false-dependence pragma
skills.pattern: a hot pipelined loop has a scalar reduction or accumulation, and the loop-carried accumulator latency prevents the requested II or blocks useful unrolling/lane parallelism
required_steps: confirm the operation is a valid reduction such as sum, min, max, bitwise operation, or another associative/commutative form
choose a lane or unroll factor that matches available memory bandwidth and resources
create partial accumulators indexed by lane
completely partition the partial accumulator array
rewrite the main loop to update partial[lane] instead of one shared accumulator
pipeline the main loop and unroll the lane loop
perform final reduction across partial accumulators
check numerical tolerance for floating-point or non-associative expressions
skills.strategy: replace the single accumulator with lane-local partial accumulators, update them in parallel, and combine them with a final tree or cleanup reduction; preserve serial order only when exact order is required

guards: do not assume coalescing succeeded without checking reports
do not expose benchmark or hidden-test provenance
do not over-unroll if the new bottleneck becomes compute resources or local memory ports
skills.pattern: narrow per-element AXI burst or scalar global-memory access on a contiguous read/write loop
required_steps: identify contiguous global-memory access
apply burst-friendly m_axi configuration when legal
stage or reshape memory access if needed
rewrite compute to exploit widened/local data when legal
handle tails and validate reports
skills.strategy: preserve the public kernel ABI by default; request max_widen_bitwidth=512 on m_axi ports; improve burst lengths, outstanding transactions, local staging, and tail-safe contiguous access; then restructure the compute loop so the wider memory beat feeds multiple parallel lane operations when legal
